Date: 11/09/2026

## GOHREP

**Goal:**

Set a baseline for the deep models. It uses the same hand-crafted features, kinds of
model and code as Chapter 2's `10b_score_prediction.qmd`. But it is evaluated on the
training, validation and test split that every model in this repository uses.

**Rationale:**

This copies the original code rather than rewriting it. Sections 1 to 6 reproduce
`10b_score_prediction.qmd` line for line. They use the same twelve features, balanced
undersample, five-fold cross validation grouped by leaf, `maxnodes` sweep,
proportional-odds ordinal regression, baselines and leakage check. So the numbers here
can be checked against the ones that analysis published. Section 7 is the only new
part. The same models are refitted on the medoid_64 training split, tuned on the
validation split and scored once on the 308 test CDAs. This makes them comparable with
models/03 and models/04.

It is written in R for the same reason as the original. `MASS::polr` fits the
proportional-odds model, and this project's Python environment has no equivalent.

**The features** are eleven segmentation features and `entropy_raw`. `frac_g_gt_r` is
deliberately NOT a model feature, because of the Otsu artefact discussed in
`10_segmentation_and_feature_extraction` section 5.2. It is kept only for the
one-feature "Threshold: CDA area" baseline.

---

## 2. Features, class balance and a leakage-safe cross validation

Copied from `10b_score_prediction.qmd` sections 2.1 to 2.3.

```{r}
# 2.1  Features and class balancing
features <- read.csv(file.path(uv_repo, "data", "features", "cda_image_features.csv"))

seg_features <- c(
  "ent_gap", "green_gap", "cda_green", "sep",
  "cda_green_sd", "cda_bright", "cda_bright_sd", "leaf_green_sd",
  "mean_green", "log_gr", "leaf_bright"
)
other_features <- c("entropy_raw")
all_features <- c(seg_features, other_features)

feat_all <- features %>%
  dplyr::select(image_id, source, score, frac_g_gt_r, dplyr::all_of(all_features))

set.seed(42)
min_n <- min(table(feat_all$score))
bal_idx <- unlist(lapply(0:6, function(s) {
  idx <- which(feat_all$score == s)
  if (length(idx) > min_n) sample(idx, min_n) else idx
}))
feat <- feat_all[bal_idx, ]
X <- as.matrix(feat[, all_features])
y <- feat$score
cat(sprintf(
  "Balanced set: %d images per class, %d total, %d features\n",
  min_n, nrow(feat), length(all_features)
))
```

```{r}
# 2.2  Source-grouped 5-fold assignment (a leaf's crops never split across folds)
K <- 5
set.seed(42)
usrc <- unique(feat$source)
src_fold <- setNames(sample(rep(1:K, length.out = length(usrc))), usrc)
fold <- unname(src_fold[feat$source])
cat(sprintf(
  "%d source leaves assigned across %d folds; fold sizes: %s\n",
  length(usrc), K, paste(as.integer(table(fold)), collapse = ", ")
))
```

```{r}
# 2.3  Leakage sanity check: shuffled labels MUST collapse to chance.
rf_reg_cv <- function(ntree, target = y) {
  pred <- numeric(length(target))
  for (f in 1:K) {
    tr <- fold != f
    te <- fold == f
    m <- randomForest::randomForest(x = X[tr, , drop = FALSE], y = target[tr], ntree = ntree)
    pred[te] <- predict(m, X[te, , drop = FALSE])
  }
  pmin(pmax(round(pred), 0), 6)
}
# Cached: five 200-tree forests on shuffled labels, and the answer cannot change unless
# the features or the folds do.
leak_cache <- file.path(analysis_dir, "model_cache", "leakage_check.rds")
if (file.exists(leak_cache)) {
  shuffle_acc <- readRDS(leak_cache)
} else {
  set.seed(7)
  y_shuffled <- sample(y)
  shuffle_acc <- mean(rf_reg_cv(200, y_shuffled) == y_shuffled)
  saveRDS(shuffle_acc, leak_cache)
}
cat(sprintf(
  "Leakage check - shuffled-label cross validation exact accuracy = %.3f (chance = %.3f)\n",
  shuffle_acc, 1 / 7
))
```

## 3. Random forest: regularising with maxnodes

```{r}
# 3.1
NTREE <- 200
rf_fit_cv <- function(maxnodes) {
  pred <- numeric(length(y))
  for (f in 1:K) {
    tr <- fold != f
    te <- fold == f
    m <- randomForest::randomForest(
      x = X[tr, , drop = FALSE], y = y[tr], ntree = NTREE, maxnodes = maxnodes
    )
    pred[te] <- predict(m, X[te, , drop = FALSE])
  }
  pmin(pmax(round(pred), 0), 6)
}
rf_fit_train <- function(maxnodes) {
  set.seed(1)
  m <- randomForest::randomForest(x = X, y = y, ntree = NTREE, maxnodes = maxnodes)
  pmin(pmax(round(predict(m, X)), 0), 6)
}
maxnodes_grid <- c(4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256)
# Cached: 7 maxnodes x (1 resubstitution fit + 5 cross-validation fits) x 200 trees, plus
# the refit at the chosen value. Deterministic given the features and the fold assignment.
reg_cache <- file.path(analysis_dir, "model_cache", "rf_regularisation.rds")
if (file.exists(reg_cache)) {
  .rc <- readRDS(reg_cache)
  reg_curve <- .rc$reg_curve
  rf_best_cached <- .rc$rf_best
} else {
  set.seed(42)
  reg_curve <- data.frame(
    maxnodes = maxnodes_grid,
    train = sapply(maxnodes_grid, function(mn) mean(rf_fit_train(mn) == y)),
    cross_validation = sapply(maxnodes_grid, function(mn) mean(rf_fit_cv(mn) == y))
  )
  reg_curve$gap <- reg_curve$train - reg_curve$cross_validation
  rf_best_cached <- rf_fit_cv(max(reg_curve$maxnodes[reg_curve$gap <= 0.15]))
  saveRDS(list(reg_curve = reg_curve, rf_best = rf_best_cached), reg_cache)
}
best_maxnodes <- max(reg_curve$maxnodes[reg_curve$gap <= 0.15])
cat(sprintf(
  "Chosen maxnodes = %d: train = %.3f, cross validation = %.3f, gap = %.3f (<= 0.15)\n",
  best_maxnodes,
  reg_curve$train[reg_curve$maxnodes == best_maxnodes],
  reg_curve$cross_validation[reg_curve$maxnodes == best_maxnodes],
  reg_curve$gap[reg_curve$maxnodes == best_maxnodes]
))
rf_best <- rf_best_cached
```

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
# 3.2
p_reg <- reg_curve %>%
  pivot_longer(c(train, cross_validation), names_to = "set", values_to = "accuracy") %>%
  ggplot(aes(maxnodes, accuracy, colour = set)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = best_maxnodes, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(train = "#B2182B", cross_validation = "#2166AC"),
    labels = c(cross_validation = "held out (grouped 5-fold cross validation)",
               train = "training"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = maxnodes_grid) +
  labs(x = "max leaf nodes per tree (log scale)", y = "Exact accuracy") +
  theme_minimal() +

        legend.position = "top")
p_reg
save_plot(p_reg, "rf_regularisation.png", width = 8, height = 4.5)
```

## 4. Ordinal regression

Proportional-odds ordinal logistic regression fits one linear combination of the twelve
features and six ordered cut-points. So the model uses the order of the scale, rather
than treating the seven scores as unrelated labels.

```{r}
# 4.1
ord_cv <- function() {
  pred <- integer(length(y))
  for (f in 1:K) {
    tr <- fold != f
    te <- fold == f
    mu <- colMeans(X[tr, ])
    sdv <- apply(X[tr, ], 2, sd)
    sdv[sdv == 0] <- 1
    dtr <- data.frame(scale(X[tr, , drop = FALSE], mu, sdv),
      y = factor(y[tr], levels = 0:6, ordered = TRUE)
    )
    dte <- data.frame(scale(X[te, , drop = FALSE], mu, sdv))
    fit <- suppressWarnings(MASS::polr(y ~ ., data = dtr, Hess = TRUE))
    pred[te] <- as.integer(as.character(predict(fit, dte, type = "class")))
  }
  pred
}
ord_train <- function() {
  mu <- colMeans(X)
  sdv <- apply(X, 2, sd)
  sdv[sdv == 0] <- 1
  d <- data.frame(scale(X, mu, sdv), y = factor(y, levels = 0:6, ordered = TRUE))
  fit <- suppressWarnings(MASS::polr(y ~ ., data = d, Hess = TRUE))
  as.integer(as.character(predict(fit, data.frame(scale(X, mu, sdv)), type = "class")))
}
ord_best <- ord_cv()
ord_tr <- ord_train()
cat(sprintf(
  "Ordinal regression: held-out exact = %.3f, near-miss = %.3f; training = %.3f, gap = %.3f\n",
  mean(ord_best == y), mean(abs(ord_best - y) <= 1),
  mean(ord_tr == y), mean(ord_tr == y) - mean(ord_best == y)
))
```

## 5. Reproduction check against 10b

If this copy is faithful, the rows below must match the values that
`10b_score_prediction.qmd` publishes. These are 0.615 for ordinal regression, 0.565 for
the random forest, 0.111 for the CDA area threshold and 0.143 for always guessing one
class.

```{r}
# 5.1
thresh_cv <- function(x) {
  pred <- integer(length(y))
  for (f in 1:K) {
    tr <- fold != f
    te <- fold == f
    med <- tapply(x[tr], y[tr], median)
    sc <- as.integer(names(med))
    o <- order(sc); med <- med[o]; sc <- sc[o]
    cuts <- cummax((head(med, -1) + tail(med, -1)) / 2)
    pred[te] <- sc[findInterval(x[te], cuts) + 1]
  }
  pred
}
thresh_train <- function(x) {
  med <- tapply(x, y, median)
  sc <- as.integer(names(med))
  o <- order(sc); med <- med[o]; sc <- sc[o]
  cuts <- cummax((head(med, -1) + tail(med, -1)) / 2)
  sc[findInterval(x, cuts) + 1]
}
maj <- rep(as.integer(names(which.max(table(y)))), length(y))

cmp_row <- function(train_pred, test_pred, name, tuning) {
  data.frame(
    model = name, tuning = tuning,
    train = mean(train_pred == y), cross_validation = mean(test_pred == y),
    gap = mean(train_pred == y) - mean(test_pred == y),
    near_miss = mean(abs(test_pred - y) <= 1)
  )
}
results <- rbind(
  cmp_row(maj, maj, "Majority class", ""),
  cmp_row(thresh_train(feat$frac_g_gt_r), thresh_cv(feat$frac_g_gt_r),
          "Threshold: CDA area", "1 feature"),
  cmp_row(ord_tr, ord_best, "Ordinal regression", "12 features"),
  cmp_row(rf_fit_train(best_maxnodes), rf_best, "Random forest",
          sprintf("%d nodes", best_maxnodes))
)
results %>%
  mutate(across(c(train, cross_validation, gap, near_miss), ~ round(., 3))) %>%
  arrange(desc(cross_validation)) %>%
  as.data.frame()
```

## 6. The medoid_64 splits

This is the only part that is not in 10b. The same two models are refitted on the
medoid_64 training split (1,834 crops), with each one's hyperparameter chosen on the
validation split (455 crops). They are then refitted on training plus validation and
scored once on the 308 test CDAs. These are the same crops that models/03 and models/04
report `test_acc` on.

```{r}
# 6.1
split <- read.csv(file.path(repo_root, "data", "datasets", "medoid_64", "medoid_64.csv"))
split$image_id <- sub("\\.tif$", "", split$filename)
d <- merge(split, feat_all, by = "image_id")
stopifnot(nrow(d) == nrow(split), all(d$label == d$score))
cat(sprintf("%d crops joined; per split: %s\n", nrow(d),
            paste(sprintf("%s=%d", names(table(d$split)), as.integer(table(d$split))),
                  collapse = ", ")))

Xtr <- as.matrix(d[d$split == "train", all_features]); ytr <- d$score[d$split == "train"]
Xva <- as.matrix(d[d$split == "val", all_features]);   yva <- d$score[d$split == "val"]
Xte <- as.matrix(d[d$split == "test", all_features]);  yte <- d$score[d$split == "test"]
Xtv <- rbind(Xtr, Xva); ytv <- c(ytr, yva)

zfit <- function(A) { mu <- colMeans(A); s <- apply(A, 2, sd); s[s == 0] <- 1; list(mu = mu, s = s) }
zap  <- function(A, p) scale(A, p$mu, p$s)

# Ordinal forest (Hornung 2020, J. Classification 37, 4-17, doi:10.1007/s00357-018-9302-x).
# A regression forest whose target is a set of SCORE VALUES optimised by out-of-bag
# performance, rather than the class values 0-6 assumed equally spaced and then rounded.
# The polr cut-points in section 9 are not equally spaced, so that assumption is measurably
# wrong on these crops, which is the reason for using it here.
of_fit <- function(Xa, ya, seed = 42) {
  set.seed(seed)
  ordinalForest::ordfor(depvar = "y",
                        data = data.frame(Xa, y = factor(ya, levels = 0:6, ordered = TRUE)),
                        perffunction = "equal")
}
of_predict <- function(fit, Xb) {
  as.integer(as.character(predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(Xb))$ypred))
}
ord_at <- function(Xa, ya, Xb) {
  p <- zfit(Xa)
  dtr <- data.frame(zap(Xa, p), y = factor(ya, levels = 0:6, ordered = TRUE))
  fit <- suppressWarnings(MASS::polr(y ~ ., data = dtr, Hess = TRUE))
  as.integer(as.character(predict(fit, data.frame(zap(Xb, p)), type = "class")))
}

# Neither model has a tuned hyperparameter: polr has none, and ordfor's defaults "were
# found to be in a reasonable range" per its documentation. Cached, because the ordinal
# forest grows 1,000 exploratory forests plus a 5,000-tree final one.
of_cache <- file.path(analysis_dir, "model_cache", "ordinal_forests.rds")
# The forest objects are ~98 MB, and reading them back costs about ten seconds even though
# nothing downstream needs the trees themselves -- only three prediction vectors and the
# permutation importances. Those are cached separately so a normal render never touches the
# large file; delete of_derived.rds to rebuild them from the forests.
of_derived <- file.path(analysis_dir, "model_cache", "ordinal_forest_outputs.rds")
if (file.exists(of_derived)) {
  ofo <- readRDS(of_derived)
} else {
  if (file.exists(of_cache)) {
    ofs <- readRDS(of_cache)
  } else {
    ofs <- list(tr = of_fit(Xtr, ytr), tv = of_fit(Xtv, ytv))
    saveRDS(ofs, of_cache)
  }
  ofo <- list(tr_on_va = of_predict(ofs$tr, Xva),
              tv_on_te = of_predict(ofs$tv, Xte),
              varimp   = ofs$tv$varimp)
  saveRDS(ofo, of_derived)
}
cat(sprintf("val accuracy -- ordinal forest %.3f, ordinal regression %.3f\n",
            mean(ofo$tr_on_va == yva), mean(ord_at(Xtr, ytr, Xva) == yva)))
```

```{r}
# 6.2
# Both splits scored the same way, so val and test near-miss are directly comparable.
score_row <- function(vpred, tpred, name, tuning) {
  data.frame(
    model = name, tuning = tuning,
    val_exact     = if (is.null(vpred)) NA else round(mean(vpred == yva), 4),
    val_near_miss = if (is.null(vpred)) NA else round(mean(abs(vpred - yva) <= 1), 4),
    test_exact     = round(mean(tpred == yte), 4),
    test_near_miss = round(mean(abs(tpred - yte) <= 1), 4)
  )
}
maj_te <- rep(as.integer(names(which.max(table(ytv)))), length(yte))
maj_va <- rep(maj_te[1], length(yva))
area_tv <- d$frac_g_gt_r[d$split %in% c("train", "val")]
area_va <- d$frac_g_gt_r[d$split == "val"]
area_te <- d$frac_g_gt_r[d$split == "test"]
med <- tapply(area_tv, ytv, median); sc <- as.integer(names(med))
o <- order(sc); med <- med[o]; sc <- sc[o]
cuts <- cummax((head(med, -1) + tail(med, -1)) / 2)

final <- rbind(
  score_row(maj_va, maj_te, "Majority class", ""),
  score_row(sc[findInterval(area_va, cuts) + 1], sc[findInterval(area_te, cuts) + 1],
            "Threshold: CDA area", "1 feature"),
  score_row(ord_at(Xtr, ytr, Xva), ord_at(Xtv, ytv, Xte),
            "Ordinal regression", "12 features"),
  score_row(ofo$tr_on_va, ofo$tv_on_te,
            "Ordinal forest", "defaults")
)
final %>% arrange(desc(test_exact)) %>% as.data.frame()

# Exported so the cross-model analysis can compare these against the deep models
# per-image, rather than refitting them there.
write.csv(
  data.frame(
    image_id = d$image_id[d$split == "test"],
    true = yte,
    ordinal_regression = ord_at(Xtv, ytv, Xte),
    ordinal_forest = ofo$tv_on_te
  ),
  file.path(analysis_dir, "model_cache", "nondl_test_predictions.csv"), row.names = FALSE
)

# The same train+val fit, applied to the ENSEMBLE split as well. analyses/14 selects and
# tunes its combiners on that split and reports test once, so it needs both. The ensemble
# crops are held out of every model in this repository, so scoring them here is not
# leakage; they are simply a second unseen split.
# Class probabilities as well as the hard score, so analyses/14 can put this model into
# probability-averaging rules on the same footing as the softmax of a network.
ord_probs_at <- function(Xa, ya, Xb) {
  p <- zfit(Xa)
  dtr <- data.frame(zap(Xa, p), y = factor(ya, levels = 0:6, ordered = TRUE))
  fit <- suppressWarnings(MASS::polr(y ~ ., data = dtr, Hess = TRUE))
  pr <- predict(fit, data.frame(zap(Xb, p)), type = "probs")
  colnames(pr) <- paste0("p", 0:6)
  pr
}
Xen <- as.matrix(d[d$split == "ensemble", all_features])
yen <- d$score[d$split == "ensemble"]
write.csv(
  rbind(
    data.frame(image_id = d$image_id[d$split == "ensemble"], split = "ensemble",
               true = yen, ordinal_regression = ord_at(Xtv, ytv, Xen),
               ord_probs_at(Xtv, ytv, Xen)),
    data.frame(image_id = d$image_id[d$split == "test"], split = "test",
               true = yte, ordinal_regression = ord_at(Xtv, ytv, Xte),
               ord_probs_at(Xtv, ytv, Xte))
  ),
  file.path(analysis_dir, "model_cache", "nondl_heldout_predictions.csv"), row.names = FALSE
)
cat(sprintf("ordinal regression: ensemble %.4f, test %.4f\n",
            mean(ord_at(Xtv, ytv, Xen) == yen), mean(ord_at(Xtv, ytv, Xte) == yte)))
```

```{r}
# 7.3  Against the deep models and the human raters, on the identical 308 test CDAs.
deep <- data.frame(
  model = c("CNN (models/03)", "ViT (models/04)", "Human raters (Chapter 2 Metric 3)"),
  tuning = c("8,640 configs", "2,592 configs", ""),
  val_exact = c(0.6457, 0.6466, NA),
  val_near_miss = c(0.9733, 0.9720, NA),
  test_exact = c(0.6169, 0.6429, 0.6892),

rbind(final, deep) %>% arrange(desc(test_exact)) %>% as.data.frame()
```

## 7. Confusion matrix of the best model

Adapted from `10b_score_prediction.qmd` section 7. It is drawn on the medoid_64 test
split rather than the grouped cross validation. It uses `_plot_confusion_matrix` from
`src/cnn_base.py`, so it matches every other confusion matrix in this project.

```{r}
# 7.1
best_name <- as.character(final$model[which.max(final$test_exact)])
best_pred <- switch(best_name,
  "Ordinal regression" = ord_at(Xtv, ytv, Xte),
  "Ordinal forest"     = ofo$tv_on_te
)
cm <- table(factor(yte, levels = 0:6), factor(best_pred, levels = 0:6))
cat(sprintf("Best on test: %s (exact %.4f)\n", best_name, mean(best_pred == yte)))
write.csv(as.data.frame.matrix(cm), file.path(analysis_dir, "model_cache",
                                              "best_model_confusion.csv"))
print(cm)
```

```{python}
# 8.2  Drawn with the project's shared plotting function.
import sys
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
repo_root = next(p for p in Path.cwd().parents if (p / ".git").exists())
sys.path.append(str(repo_root / "src"))

cm_csv = Path("model_cache") / "best_model_confusion.csv"
cm = pd.read_csv(cm_csv, index_col=0).to_numpy()
out = Path("thesis_plots") / "best_nondl_confusion_matrix.png"
# `cnn_base` imports TensorFlow at module level, which costs about 14 s for a function that
# only draws a matrix. The import is skipped when the PNG already corresponds to these exact
# counts, tracked by a hash sidecar rather than mtimes -- the counts CSV is rewritten every
# render, so an mtime test would never fire.
import hashlib as _hl
_sig = _hl.sha256(cm.tobytes()).hexdigest()
_sigfile = out.with_suffix(".sha256")
if out.exists() and _sigfile.exists() and _sigfile.read_text().strip() == _sig:
    print(f"{out.name} already matches these counts; kept, TensorFlow import skipped")
else:
    from cnn_base import _plot_confusion_matrix  # noqa: E402
    _plot_confusion_matrix(cm, np.arange(7), ("True score", "Predicted score"), str(out))
    _sigfile.write_text(_sig)
print(f"{cm.sum()} test crops; {np.trace(cm)} correct ({np.trace(cm) / cm.sum():.4f})")
```

## 8. Ordinal forest: regularisation sweep and importance

The same sweep as for the regression forest in section 3, on the ordinal forest's
capacity setting. `ordfor` passes `min.node.size` to ranger. A larger minimum node size
means smaller trees, so it does the job of `maxnodes` there, in the opposite direction.
Training accuracy is measured on the training data. Held-out accuracy is on the
medoid_64 validation split.

```{r}
# 8.1
of_cache2 <- file.path(analysis_dir, "model_cache", "ordinal_forest_sweep.rds")
mns_grid <- c(1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100)
if (file.exists(of_cache2)) {
  of_curve <- readRDS(of_cache2)
} else {
  of_at <- function(mns, Xa, ya, Xb) {
    set.seed(42)
    m <- ordinalForest::ordfor(depvar = "y",
                               data = data.frame(Xa, y = factor(ya, levels = 0:6, ordered = TRUE)),
                               perffunction = "equal", min.node.size = mns)
    as.integer(as.character(predict(m, newdata = data.frame(Xb))$ypred))
  }
  of_curve <- data.frame(
    min_node_size = mns_grid,
    train = sapply(mns_grid, function(m) mean(of_at(m, Xtr, ytr, Xtr) == ytr)),
    held_out = sapply(mns_grid, function(m) mean(of_at(m, Xtr, ytr, Xva) == yva))
  )
  saveRDS(of_curve, of_cache2)
}
of_curve$gap <- of_curve$train - of_curve$held_out
best_mns <- of_curve$min_node_size[which.max(of_curve$held_out)]
cat(sprintf("Chosen min.node.size = %d: train = %.3f, held out = %.3f, gap = %.3f\n",
            best_mns, of_curve$train[of_curve$min_node_size == best_mns],
            of_curve$held_out[of_curve$min_node_size == best_mns],
            of_curve$gap[of_curve$min_node_size == best_mns]))
print(of_curve, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
# 8.2
p_ofreg <- of_curve %>%
  pivot_longer(c(train, held_out), names_to = "set", values_to = "accuracy") %>%
  ggplot(aes(min_node_size, accuracy, colour = set)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = best_mns, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(train = "#B2182B", held_out = "#2166AC"),
                      labels = c(held_out = "Held out (validation split)", train = "Training"),
                      name = NULL) +
  # min.node.size runs the opposite way to the random forest's maxnodes: ranger's
  # "minimal node size to split at" means a LARGER value stops splitting sooner, so it is
  # less capacity, not more. The axis is reversed so both sweeps read left-to-right as
  # increasing capacity and the two curves are directly comparable.
  scale_x_continuous(trans = scales::compose_trans("log10", "reverse"),
                     breaks = mns_grid) +
  labs(x = "Minimum node size to split at (log scale, reversed: capacity increases rightwards)",
       y = "Exact accuracy") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 12), axis.title = element_text(size = 13),
        legend.position = "top")
p_ofreg
save_plot(p_ofreg, "ordinal_forest_sweep.png", width = 8, height = 4.5)
```

```{r fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
# 8.3  Permutation importance from the fitted ordinal forest.
imp_df <- data.frame(feature = pretty_feature(names(ofo$varimp)),
                     importance = as.numeric(ofo$varimp))
p_imp <- ggplot(imp_df, aes(x = reorder(feature, importance), y = importance)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2166AC") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Ordinal forest permutation importance") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 12), axis.title = element_text(size = 13))
p_imp
save_plot(p_imp, "ordinal_forest_importance.png", width = 7, height = 5)
```

## 8b. Confusion matrix as a change from the human baseline

The model and human matrices look alike, because both have most of their counts near the
diagonal. Subtracting one from the other shows where they differ. Each cell is the model's
row proportion minus the human row proportion. Red means the model does that more often
than a rater, and blue less often. The counts cannot be compared directly, because there
are 917 rater judgements and 308 model predictions. So each row is normalised first.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Best non-DL model minus human raters, as a change in row proportion on the 308 test CDAs."
# 8b.1
import sys as _s
from pathlib import Path as _Pth
import numpy as _np, pandas as _pd, matplotlib.pyplot as _plt
from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle as _Rect

# repo_root is the Python variable set in chunk 8.2; reticulate keeps one Python session
# for the whole document, so it is still in scope here.
_hum = _pd.read_csv(repo_root / "analyses/02_human_performance/thesis_plots/human_confusion_matrix.csv",
                    index_col=0).to_numpy(dtype=float)
_mod = _pd.read_csv(_Pth("model_cache") / "best_model_confusion.csv", index_col=0).to_numpy(dtype=float)
# The human matrix carries an eighth column, the tautological judgements Metric 3
# removes. They must stay in the row totals: without them the denominator is 875 and
# row-normalising gives a human diagonal of 72.23%, against the 68.92% Metric 3
# reports over all 917. A model has no such category, so its matrix is padded with a
# zero column and the two are then directly comparable.
_mod = _np.hstack([_mod, _np.zeros((7, 1))])
_hn = _hum / _np.clip(_hum.sum(1, keepdims=True), 1, None)
_mn = _mod / _np.clip(_mod.sum(1, keepdims=True), 1, None)
_diff = _mn - _hn

_fig, _ax = _plt.subplots(figsize=(6.9, 5.2))
_v = _np.abs(_diff).max()
_im = _ax.imshow(_diff, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-_v, vmax=_v)
for i in range(7):
    for j in range(8):
        if abs(_diff[i, j]) > 0.005:
            _ax.text(j, i, f"{_diff[i, j]:+.2f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7,
                     color="white" if abs(_diff[i, j]) > 0.6 * _v else "black")
        if i == j:
            _ax.add_patch(_Rect((j - 0.5, i - 0.5), 1, 1, fill=False, edgecolor="black", lw=_plt.rcParams["axes.linewidth"]))
_ax.set_xticks(range(8), [*range(7), "taut."]); _ax.set_yticks(range(7))
_ax.set_xlabel("Predicted score"); _ax.set_ylabel("True score")
_fig.colorbar(_im, ax=_ax, fraction=0.046, label="Model minus human (row proportion)")
_fig.savefig(_Pth("thesis_plots") / "nondl_confusion_vs_human.png", dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
_plt.show()
print(f"diagonal change: {_np.diag(_diff).round(3)}")
```

## 9. Ordinal regression: what the fitted model looks like

Four candidate figures for the chapter, all read directly from the fitted `polr` model
(training plus validation, 2,289 crops). None needs SHAP, because a proportional-odds
model shows its coefficients and cut-points directly.

```{r}
# 10.1  Refit on train+val and pull out the pieces the plots need.
p_tv  <- zfit(Xtv)
Ztv   <- data.frame(zap(Xtv, p_tv), y = factor(ytv, levels = 0:6, ordered = TRUE))
ord_fit <- suppressWarnings(MASS::polr(y ~ ., data = Ztv, Hess = TRUE))
ct    <- coef(summary(ord_fit))
betas <- data.frame(
  feature = rownames(ct)[seq_along(all_features)],
  value   = ct[seq_along(all_features), "Value"],
  se      = ct[seq_along(all_features), "Std. Error"],
  t       = ct[seq_along(all_features), "t value"]
)
zeta  <- ord_fit$zeta
lp_tv <- as.numeric(as.matrix(zap(Xtv, p_tv)) %*% coef(ord_fit))
cat("cut-points:\n"); print(round(zeta, 3))
cat("spacing:\n"); print(round(diff(zeta), 3))
```

### 10.1 Coefficients

The ordinal model's counterpart to the random forest's Gini panel. It shows direction
and significance, which Gini does not. Each bar is the effect of one standard deviation
of a standardised feature, in log-odds.

```{r fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
# 10.2
p_coef <- betas %>%
  mutate(feature = reorder(pretty_feature(feature), value)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(value, feature)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = value - 1.96 * se, xmax = value + 1.96 * se), height = 0.25,
                 colour = "#2166AC") +
  geom_point(colour = "#2166AC", size = 2) +
  labs(x = "Coefficient (log-odds per SD, 95% CI)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 12), axis.title = element_text(size = 13))
p_coef
save_plot(p_coef, "ordinal_coefficients.png", width = 7, height = 5)
```

### 10.2 Cut-points on the latent scale

The six thresholds the model sets on its single hidden severity score, with each crop's
hidden score shown underneath. This shows the boundaries between consecutive scores
directly, rather than inferring them.

```{r fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
# 10.3
lat <- data.frame(lp = lp_tv, score = factor(ytv, levels = 0:6))
# Label the band each cut-point pair encloses, not the boundaries themselves: the score a
# crop is given is decided by which band its latent score falls in. The outer two bands are
# unbounded, so the data range stands in for their outer edge.
band_edges <- c(min(lat$lp), zeta, max(lat$lp))
band_mids  <- (head(band_edges, -1) + tail(band_edges, -1)) / 2
p_cut <- ggplot(lat, aes(lp, score)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = zeta, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30") +
  geom_jitter(aes(colour = score), height = 0.22, alpha = 0.45, size = 0.9,
              show.legend = FALSE) +
  annotate("text", x = band_mids, y = 7.75, label = 0:6, size = 4.6, vjust = 0,
           fontface = "plain", colour = "grey20") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.5, 8.3), clip = "off") +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(option = "viridis", end = 0.9) +
  labs(x = "Latent severity score (linear predictor)", y = "True score") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 12), axis.title = element_text(size = 13),
        plot.margin = margin(20, 10, 5, 5))
p_cut
save_plot(p_cut, "ordinal_cutpoints.png", width = 9, height = 4.5)
```

### 10.3 Class-probability curves

How the predicted probability of each score changes along the hidden scale. Under
proportional odds, the seven curves are shifted copies of one shape. This plot shows it
rather than assuming it.

```{r fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
# 10.4
grid_lp <- seq(min(lp_tv) - 1, max(lp_tv) + 1, length.out = 400)
cum <- sapply(zeta, function(z) plogis(z - grid_lp))       # P(Y <= k | lp)
probs <- cbind(cum[, 1], t(apply(cum, 1, diff)), 1 - cum[, ncol(cum)])
colnames(probs) <- 0:6
p_prob <- as.data.frame(probs) %>%
  mutate(lp = grid_lp) %>%
  pivot_longer(-lp, names_to = "score", values_to = "p") %>%
  ggplot(aes(lp, p, colour = score)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = zeta, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey70") +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(option = "viridis", end = 0.9) +
  labs(x = "Latent severity score (linear predictor)", y = "Predicted probability",
       colour = "Score") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 12), axis.title = element_text(size = 13),
        legend.position = "top")
p_prob
save_plot(p_prob, "ordinal_class_probabilities.png", width = 9, height = 4.5)
```

### 10.4 Effect of the three strongest features

The predicted probability of each score as one feature varies across its observed range,
with every other feature held at its mean.

```{r fig.width=11, fig.height=4}
# 10.5
top3 <- betas$feature[order(-abs(betas$t))][1:3]
eff <- lapply(top3, function(v) {
  base <- colMeans(zap(Xtv, p_tv))
  rng  <- range(zap(Xtv, p_tv)[, v])
  gs   <- seq(rng[1], rng[2], length.out = 150)
  M <- matrix(rep(base, each = length(gs)), nrow = length(gs))
  colnames(M) <- names(base); M[, v] <- gs
  lp <- as.numeric(M %*% coef(ord_fit))
  cum <- sapply(zeta, function(z) plogis(z - lp))
  pr <- cbind(cum[, 1], t(apply(cum, 1, diff)), 1 - cum[, ncol(cum)])
  colnames(pr) <- 0:6
  as.data.frame(pr) %>% mutate(x = gs, feature = v) %>%
    pivot_longer(-c(x, feature), names_to = "score", values_to = "p")
}) %>% bind_rows()
p_eff <- ggplot(eff, aes(x, p, colour = score)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~feature, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(option = "viridis", end = 0.9) +
  labs(x = "Feature value (standardised)", y = "Predicted probability", colour = "Score") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 11), axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
        legend.position = "top")
p_eff
save_plot(p_eff, "ordinal_effects.png", width = 11, height = 4)
```

## 10. Summary against the deep models and human raters

Exact accuracy, with near-miss accuracy stacked on top. Each bar's full height is the
near-miss accuracy, and the solid part is the exact accuracy. The augmented and ensemble
models use the same layout.

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
# 10.1
summ <- rbind(final, deep) %>%
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = model[order(-test_exact)])) %>%
  transmute(model,
            Exact = test_exact,
            `Off by one` = test_near_miss - test_exact) %>%
  pivot_longer(-model, names_to = "band", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(band = factor(band, levels = c("Off by one", "Exact")))

# Upright bars, so the models run along the x axis and the shared 0-1 proportion is the
# vertical scale. The human exact line is named in a legend rather than written along it.
# Shortened only on the axis: the rotated full names run off the left of a fixed-width
# ggsave, and the model provenance belongs in the prose rather than on a tick.
short <- c("Human raters (Chapter 2 Metric 3)" = "Human raters",
           "CNN (models/03)" = "CNN", "ViT (models/04)" = "ViT",
           "Threshold: CDA area" = "CDA area threshold")
summ <- summ %>% mutate(model = factor(dplyr::recode(as.character(model), !!!short),
                                       levels = dplyr::recode(levels(model), !!!short)))

p_summ <- ggplot(summ, aes(model, value, fill = band)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 0.6892, linetype = "Human exact (0.689)"),
             colour = "grey30") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Exact = "#2166AC", `Off by one` = "#92C5DE"), name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Human exact (0.689)" = "dashed"), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Proportion of the 308 test CDAs") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 11), axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "top")
p_summ
save_plot(p_summ, "summary_vs_human.png", width = 8, height = 5.2)
```
